\chapter{Communication Complexity --- Discrepancy}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.CommunicationComplexity.NewmanTheorem.Discrepancy
\section{Overview}

This module establishes the \emph{discrepancy method} lower bound for public-coin
communication complexity.  The central definition is the discrepancy of a Boolean
function $g : X \to Y \to \mathrm{Bool}$ on a combinatorial rectangle $R \subseteq X
\times Y$ with respect to a distribution $\mu$; the main result is that if every
rectangle has discrepancy at most $\gamma$, then the (public-coin) communication
complexity of $g$ must be large.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Discrepancy of a Boolean function]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.discrepancy}
\statementsource{raoyehudayoff-ch05-discrepancy}{pdf-4c44440f2aaa-p001-b002}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.discrepancy}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.FiniteProbabilitySpace, CommunicationComplexity.boolSign}
Let $\mu$ be a finite probability space on $X \times Y$, let $g : X \to Y \to
\mathrm{Bool}$, and let $S \subseteq X \times Y$.  The \emph{discrepancy} of $g$ on $S$
with respect to $\mu$ is
\[
  \mathrm{disc}_\mu(g, S)
  \;=\;
  \mathbb{E}_{(x,y)\sim\mu}\bigl[\mathbf{1}_{S}(x,y)\cdot\sigma(g(x,y))\bigr],
\]
where $\sigma : \mathrm{Bool} \to \{-1,1\}$ is the sign map \texttt{CommunicationComplexity.boolSign}.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Discrepancy integrand as a signed indicator difference]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.discrepancy_integrand_eq}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.discrepancy_integrand_eq}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.boolSign}
\difficulty{2}
Let $X$ and $Y$ be arbitrary types, let $g : X \times Y \to \mathrm{Bool}$ (written
$g(x,y)$), let $S \subseteq X \times Y$, and let $\sigma : \mathrm{Bool} \to \bbr$ send
$\mathrm{false}$ to $1$ and $\mathrm{true}$ to $-1$. Then for every point $(x,y) \in X
\times Y$,
\[
\mathbf{1}_{S}(x,y)\,\sigma\bigl(g(x,y)\bigr)
= \mathbf{1}_{\{(x,y)\in S \,:\, g(x,y)=\mathrm{false}\}}(x,y)
- \mathbf{1}_{\{(x,y)\in S \,:\, g(x,y)=\mathrm{true}\}}(x,y),
\]
where each indicator takes the value $1$ on its set and $0$ elsewhere.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Discrepancy as a difference of probabilities]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.discrepancy_eq_prob_false_sub_prob_true}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.discrepancy_eq_prob_false_sub_prob_true}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.FiniteProbabilitySpace, CommunicationComplexity.FiniteProbabilitySpace.measureReal_eq_integral_indicator_one, CommunicationComplexity.boolSign, CommunicationComplexity.discrepancy, CommunicationComplexity.discrepancy_integrand_eq}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\mu$ be a finite probability space on the product $X \times Y$, let $g : X \times Y
\to \mathrm{Bool}$, and let $S \subseteq X \times Y$. Then the discrepancy of $g$ on $S$
satisfies
\[
  \mathrm{disc}_\mu(g, S)
  \;=\;
  \mu\bigl(\{(x,y) \in S : g(x,y) = \mathrm{false}\}\bigr)
  \;-\;
  \mu\bigl(\{(x,y) \in S : g(x,y) = \mathrm{true}\}\bigr),
\]
that is, the probability mass inside $S$ on which $g$ is $\mathrm{false}$ minus the
probability mass inside $S$ on which $g$ is $\mathrm{true}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Discrepancy bound is nonnegative]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.nonneg_of_discrepancy_bound}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.nonneg_of_discrepancy_bound}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.FiniteProbabilitySpace, CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.IsRectangle, CommunicationComplexity.discrepancy}
\difficulty{2}
Let $X \times Y$ carry a finite probability space $\mu$, let $g : X \to Y \to
\mathrm{Bool}$ be a Boolean function, and let $\gamma \in \bbr$. If every rectangle $R
\subseteq X \times Y$ satisfies $\abs{\mathrm{disc}_\mu(g, R)} \le \gamma$, then $\gamma
\ge 0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Rectangle sign]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.rectangleSign}
\statementsource{raoyehudayoff-ch05-discrepancy}{pdf-4c44440f2aaa-p002-b001}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.rectangleSign}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.run}
For a deterministic Boolean protocol $p$ and a set $R \subseteq X \times Y$, the
\emph{rectangle sign} is $+1$ if the protocol outputs $\mathrm{false}$ on every point of
$R$, and $-1$ otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Rectangle sign has absolute value one]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.rectangleSign_abs}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.rectangleSign_abs}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.rectangleSign}
\difficulty{2}
Let $p$ be a deterministic Boolean two-party communication protocol on input types $X$
(Alice) and $Y$ (Bob), and let $R \subseteq X \times Y$ be any set. Define the rectangle
sign of $p$ on $R$ to be $+1$ when $p$ outputs $\mathrm{false}$ at every point of $R$
and $-1$ otherwise. Then the rectangle sign has absolute value $1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Rectangle sign equals Boolean sign on leaf rectangles]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.rectangleSign_eq_boolSign}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.rectangleSign_eq_boolSign}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectangles, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectangles_mono, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.rectangleSign, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.run, CommunicationComplexity.boolSign}
\difficulty{4}
Let $p$ be a deterministic two-party communication protocol with Boolean output, over
input types $X$ (Alice) and $Y$ (Bob). If $R$ is a leaf rectangle of $p$ and $(x, y)$ is
any point of $R$, then the rectangle sign of $R$ agrees with the Boolean sign of the
value that $p$ computes on $(x, y)$: it equals $+1$ when $p$ outputs $\mathrm{false}$ at
$(x, y)$ and $-1$ when $p$ outputs $\mathrm{true}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Finite set of leaf rectangles]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectanglesFinset}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectanglesFinset}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectangles, CommunicationComplexity.FiniteProbabilitySpace}
Given a finite probability space $\mu$ on $X \times Y$ and a deterministic protocol $p$,
this is the canonical \texttt{Finset} enumerating the (finitely many) leaf rectangles of
$p$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Membership in the finite set of leaf rectangles]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.mem_leafRectanglesFinset}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.mem_leafRectanglesFinset}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectangles, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectanglesFinset, CommunicationComplexity.FiniteProbabilitySpace}
\difficulty{1}
Let $X \times Y$ carry the structure of a finite probability space, let $p$ be a
deterministic two-party communication protocol on inputs $X$ (Alice) and $Y$ (Bob) with
Boolean output, and let $R \subseteq X \times Y$. Then $R$ belongs to the finite set
enumerating the leaf rectangles of $p$ if and only if $R$ is a leaf rectangle of $p$.
\end{lemma}

\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectanglesFinset, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectangles_isMonoPartition, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.mem_leafRectanglesFinset, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.rectangleSign, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.rectangleSign_eq_boolSign, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.run, CommunicationComplexity.FiniteProbabilitySpace, CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.monoPartition_part_unique, CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.monoPartition_point_mem, CommunicationComplexity.boolSign}
\difficulty{4}
Let $X$ and $Y$ be input types whose product $X \times Y$ carries a finite probability
space, and let $p$ be a deterministic Boolean two-party protocol over $X$ (Alice) and
$Y$ (Bob). Write $\{R\}$ for the finite collection of leaf rectangles of $p$, and for
each such rectangle assign the sign $\varepsilon(R) = +1$ if $p$ outputs
$\mathrm{false}$ at every point of $R$ and $\varepsilon(R) = -1$ otherwise. Then for
every point $(x,y) \in X \times Y$,
\[
\sum_{R} \mathbf{1}_R(x,y)\,\varepsilon(R) \;=\; \begin{cases} 1 & \text{if } p(x,y) =
\mathrm{false},\\ -1 & \text{if } p(x,y) = \mathrm{true},\end{cases}
\]
where $p(x,y)$ denotes the Boolean value returned by running $p$ on inputs $x$ and $y$.
\end{lemma}

  {CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.distributionalError}
  {context}
  {raoyehudayoff-ch05-discrepancy}
  {pdf-4c44440f2aaa-p002-b002}
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.distributionalError, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.run, CommunicationComplexity.FiniteProbabilitySpace, CommunicationComplexity.FiniteProbabilitySpace.measureReal_eq_integral_indicator_one, CommunicationComplexity.boolSign, CommunicationComplexity.boolSign_mul_boolSign_eq_sub_two_indicator}
\difficulty{4}
Let $X$ and $Y$ be the input types of Alice and Bob, and let $\mu$ be a finite
probability measure on $X \times Y$. Write $\sigma \colon \mathrm{Bool} \to \{\pm 1\}$
for the map sending $\mathrm{false}$ to $1$ and $\mathrm{true}$ to $-1$. For a
deterministic communication protocol $p$ with Boolean output and a target function $g
\colon X \to Y \to \mathrm{Bool}$, the expected signed correlation between the
protocol's output and the target satisfies
\[
  \E_{(x,y)\sim\mu}\bigl[\sigma\bigl(p(x,y)\bigr)\,\sigma\bigl(g(x,y)\bigr)\bigr]
  \;=\; 1 - 2\,\varepsilon_\mu(p,g),
\]
where $p(x,y)$ denotes the value computed by running $p$ on $(x,y)$ and
$\varepsilon_\mu(p,g) = \mu\bigl(\{(x,y) \mid p(x,y) \ne g(x,y)\}\bigr)$ is the
distributional error of $p$ against $g$ under $\mu$.
\end{lemma}

\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectanglesFinset, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.rectangleSign, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.run, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.sum_indicator_leafRectangles_eq, CommunicationComplexity.FiniteProbabilitySpace, CommunicationComplexity.boolSign, CommunicationComplexity.discrepancy}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\mu$ be a finite probability space on $X \times Y$, let $p$ be a deterministic
Boolean communication protocol with input types $X$ and $Y$, and let $g : X \to Y \to
\mathrm{Bool}$. Writing $\sigma$ for the sign map sending $\mathrm{false}$ to $1$ and
$\mathrm{true}$ to $-1$, the signed bias of $p$ against $g$ satisfies
\[
  \E_{(x,y)\sim\mu}\bigl[\sigma\bigl(p(x,y)\bigr)\cdot\sigma\bigl(g(x,y)\bigr)\bigr]
  \;=\;
  \sum_{R}\; s(p,R)\,\cdot\,\mathrm{disc}_\mu(g,R),
\]
where the sum runs over the (finitely many) leaf rectangles $R$ of $p$, the value
$p(x,y)$ is the output of $p$ on inputs $x$ and $y$, the rectangle sign $s(p,R)$ equals
$+1$ if $p$ outputs $\mathrm{false}$ at every point of $R$ and $-1$ otherwise, and
$\mathrm{disc}_\mu(g,R) = \E_{(x,y)\sim\mu}[\mathbf{1}_R(x,y)\cdot\sigma(g(x,y))]$ is
the discrepancy of $g$ on $R$.
\end{lemma}

\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.complexity, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.distributionalError, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectangles, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectanglesFinset, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectangles_card, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.leafRectangles_isRectangle, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.mem_leafRectanglesFinset, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.nonneg_of_discrepancy_bound, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.rectangleSign, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.rectangleSign_abs, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.run, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.signedBias_eq_one_sub_two_distributionalError, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.signedBias_eq_sum_rectangles, CommunicationComplexity.FiniteProbabilitySpace, CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.IsRectangle, CommunicationComplexity.boolSign, CommunicationComplexity.discrepancy}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\mu$ be a finite probability measure on $X \times Y$, let $g : X \times Y \to
\mathrm{Bool}$, and let $\gamma \in \bbr$ be such that every rectangle $R \subseteq X
\times Y$ satisfies $\abs{\mathrm{disc}_\mu(g, R)} \le \gamma$. Then for every
deterministic Boolean-valued communication protocol $p$, writing $\mathrm{err}$ for the
$\mu$-probability that $p$ disagrees with $g$ (that is, the measure of $\{(x,y) : p(x,y)
\ne g(x,y)\}$) and $c$ for the communication complexity of $p$,
\[
  1 - 2\,\mathrm{err} \;\le\; 2^{c}\cdot\gamma .
\]
\end{theorem}

\proofstep
  {CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.one_sub_two_distributionalError_le_two_pow_mul}
  {direct}
  {raoyehudayoff-ch05-discrepancy}
  {pdf-4c44440f2aaa-p002-b001,
    pdf-4c44440f2aaa-p002-b002}
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.complexity, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.distributionalError, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.one_sub_two_distributionalError_le_two_pow_mul, CommunicationComplexity.FiniteProbabilitySpace, CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.IsRectangle, CommunicationComplexity.discrepancy}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\mu$ be a finite probability space on $X \times Y$, let $g : X \times Y \to
\mathrm{Bool}$ be a Boolean function, and let $\gamma > 0$ be a real number such that
every combinatorial rectangle $R \subseteq X \times Y$ satisfies
$\abs{\mathrm{disc}_\mu(g, R)} \le \gamma$, where $\mathrm{disc}_\mu(g, R) =
\E_{(x,y)\sim\mu}[\mathbf{1}_R(x,y)\,\sigma(g(x,y))]$ and $\sigma(\mathrm{false}) = 1$,
$\sigma(\mathrm{true}) = -1$. Let $p$ be a deterministic communication protocol with
Boolean outputs, and let $\varepsilon = \mu(\{(x,y) : p(x,y) \ne g(x,y)\})$ be its
distributional error in computing $g$ under $\mu$. If $1 - 2\varepsilon > 0$, then the
communication complexity of $p$ satisfies
\[
  \log_2\!\left(\frac{1 - 2\varepsilon}{\gamma}\right) \;\le\; \mathrm{complexity}(p).
\]
\end{theorem}

\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.complexity, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.distributionalError, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.one_sub_two_distributionalError_le_two_pow_mul, CommunicationComplexity.FiniteProbabilitySpace, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.communicationComplexity, CommunicationComplexity.PublicCoin.lt_communicationComplexity_of_forall_distributionalError_gt, CommunicationComplexity.Rectangle.IsRectangle, CommunicationComplexity.discrepancy}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\mu$ be a finite probability space on $X \times Y$, let $g : X \to Y \to
\mathrm{Bool}$, and let $\varepsilon, \gamma \in \bbr$ and $n \in \bbn$. Suppose that
every rectangle $R = A \times B \subseteq X \times Y$ satisfies
$\abs{\mathrm{disc}_\mu(g, R)} \le \gamma$, where $\mathrm{disc}_\mu(g, R) =
\E_{(x,y)\sim\mu}\bigl[\mathbf{1}_R(x,y)\cdot\sigma(g(x,y))\bigr]$ and $\sigma$ sends
$\mathrm{false}$ to $1$ and $\mathrm{true}$ to $-1$. If moreover $2^n \cdot \gamma < 1 -
2\varepsilon$, then $n < \mathrm{R}^{\mathrm{pub}}_\varepsilon(g)$, the
$\varepsilon$-error public-coin randomized communication complexity of $g$.
\end{theorem}
